title: Duration.reconfigure keeps old factors when conversionAccuracy changes
body:
**Describe the bug**

When we switch `conversionAccuracy` with `Duration.reconfigure` using the default matrix, the label changes but conversions keep the old factors.

**To Reproduce**

```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund luxon@3.7.2
node -e "const { Duration } = require('luxon'); const d = Duration.fromObject({ years: 1 }).reconfigure({ conversionAccuracy: 'longterm' }); console.log(d.conversionAccuracy, d.as('days'));"
```

**Actual vs Expected behavior**

We get `longterm 365` with the [current implementation](https://github.com/moment/luxon/blob/f427515a38f6a671f8de663e6bcc040ed81f114e/src/duration.js#L127-L136).
Expected `longterm 365.2425`, per the [guide's example and table](https://github.com/moment/luxon/blob/f427515a38f6a671f8de663e6bcc040ed81f114e/docs/math.md#L231-L257).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

Version: Luxon 3.7.2 from npm. Source build f427515a38f6a671f8de663e6bcc040ed81f114e also reproduces on Node 22.20.0 and 18.20.8, Linux x86_64. Timezone irrelevant.

**Additional context**

It looks like [`clone`](https://github.com/moment/luxon/blob/f427515a38f6a671f8de663e6bcc040ed81f114e/src/duration.js#L127-L136) forwards the old matrix, which [overrides the new preset](https://github.com/moment/luxon/blob/f427515a38f6a671f8de663e6bcc040ed81f114e/src/duration.js#L187-L192).

— [ChipLab](https://chiplab.donmakino.com/findings#clab-2026-1221)
